source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Leviticus 18–20. Complete original XML records include annotation notes at 18:17, 19:1 and 20:2; no numbering shift occurs in this batch.

key_decisions.decision: Retains native/foreigner scope, offspring, death and the community's stoning action; no fire rite is inserted into the verse.
Keeps family under divine opposition but does not automatically equate every family member with the followers who are cut off; retains the sexual metaphor.
Distinguishes consultation from the practitioners in verse 27, keeping the metaphor, face image and divine agent of cutting off.
Retains both parental alternatives, the repeated offense and death responsibility image; does not weaken cursing to ordinary disagreement.
Preserves the pinned Hebrew's repeated adultery clause rather than following a shortened comparator reading; explicitly retains male and female penalty subjects.
Keeps the sexual act, father's-wife relation, father-linked nakedness and both-person capital penalty without adding consent qualifications absent from the verse.
Retains the daughter-in-law relation and the repeated blood formula; tevel agrees with 18:23 without changing the specified persons into an abstract category.
Preserves male specificity, comparison, both participants and capital penalty without adding a modern identity label or an unstated restriction on context.
Retains take and all three people in the burning penalty; does not repair the difficult rule by replacing the women with only the later partner, and notes marital/sexual scope.
Keeps human capital penalty and the separately commanded animal killing rather than generalizing the result to punishment.
Preserves female and animal roles, the direct command and repeated death/blood formula, including the source's difficult joint scope.
Keeps both sibling alternatives, reciprocal seeing, public cutting off and final male guilt; interprets hesed here as disgrace, not covenant kindness.
Preserves menstrual condition, the double fountain image and differentiated actors; does not silently replace the source with a generic impurity rule.
Identifies aunt by marriage from the uncle clause and preserves die-childless rather than silently matching the following verse's be-childless wording.
Keeps take open to marital/sexual possession, niddah's impurity sense and be-childless; does not insert an exception absent from the verse.
Preserves the pinned singular nation against pluralizing comparators, all-these-things and the force of divine disgust.
Preserves reversed clean/unclean order for birds and the shared separation verb; clarifies that the final relative clause concerns the creatures, not the ground.
Preserves has-in-them wording and both sexes rather than merely repeating consultation in verse 6; retains stoning and the concluding blood formula with a note on practitioner terminology.
